Allman Position: Aviation Attorney Education: Western State University College of Law San Diego California United States of America 1987 Chapman College 1976 M.B.A. University of Texas Austin 1966 B.A. Admitted: California 1988 Texas 1995 U.S. District Court Southern District of California 1988 Narrative: An attorney former Naval Aviator and commercial airline pilot with extensive experience in aviation law and the commercial airline industry John C. Rusty Allman s practice includes air crash litigation enforcement proceedings and aviation labor law. For 20 years Allman served as U.S. Naval Aviator flying attack and fighter aircraft from Pacific fleet aircraft carriers. He flew numerous combat missions in Viet Nam served as a Top Gun fighter pilot and later became commanding officer of the Navy s largest jet training squadron based in Pensacola Florida. He attained the final rank of Commander. During his military career he amassed over 4000 jet flight hours and 400 aircraft carrier landings. To date he has over 10000 combined flight hours. Near the end of his naval career Allman received his law degree in 1987 from Western State University now Thomas Jefferson School of Law in San Diego California. After leaving the service he flew commercially for a major U.S. airline and achieved type ratings on the Lear Jet Fokker FK-28 and Boeing 757/767. A Top Gun In the event of air crash cases Allman provides experienced insight into why things went wrong. He understands what can go on in the cockpit of an airplane how pilots react to specific situations and how the interactions of the flight crew air-traffic control and external factors affect flight safety. In addition to cockpit knowledge Allman has served on a number of accident-investigation boards deepening his knowledge of events that contribute to air crashes. Currently Allman is litigating cases in five states and serves on the plaintiffs steering committee for American Airlines 587 which crashed near Queens New York November 2001. In 2002 he worked with Michael L. Slack to negotiate a multimillion-dollar settlement agreement between the State of Alaska and three families of Air National Guardsmen who died in a crash in 1992. Expert Mediator During his career Allman has represented pilots flight attendants and aircraft mechanics in civil cases that include employment and labor contract disputes FAA certificate actions NTSB Petitions and FAA and NTSB enforcement proceedings. He has successfully mediated numerous employment and labor disputes. For example as grievance chairman for the 5000 pilots at a commercial airline he was instrumental in reducing a backlog of nearly 200 grievances while obtaining nearly $30 million for the pilots in settlement and arbitration awards. And as consultant to the National Mediation Board Allman designed a nationwide grievance mediation training program for the airline industry. He is licensed to practice law in both California and Texas. Prior to obtaining his law degree Allman received his MBA from Chapman College in 1976 and his BA from the University of Texas at Austin in 1966. Whether helping an individual develop a visitation schedule after divorce or helping a company develop a strategy for an employee or litigation issue Nola ensures she understands your desired result so everyone keeps their eye on the end goal. Nola s work is not done until you get results that make sense for you. Employment Law Nola devotes substantial time to assisting employers in tackling both day-to-day employment law issues and litigation. Nola regularly counsels employers on various compliance issues including Title VII the ADEA the FMLA the ADA the WARN Act the Affordable Care Act the Fair Credit Reporting Act wage payment collection and unemployment insurance. In addition Nola regularly drafts and reviews employee handbooks drug testing policies non-compete agreements independent contractor agreements and the various notices required under state and federal employment laws. Although Nola believes her job is to avoid litigation for her clients when litigation is unavoidable Nola represents employers before administrative agencies and state and federal trial and appellate courts. Benrubi has developed a well-earned reputation over the years as an attorney who keeps insurance companies in check. His practice is focused solely on representing policyholders in every manner of dispute involving insurance claims and in early 2016 he brought that expertise to Rosenthal Levy Simon & Ryles when he joined the firm as an counsel attorney. Mr. Benrubi launched his legal career in 1988 after receiving his J.D. from the University of Florida. He worked in a small Fort Lauderdale insurance-defense firm and then joined the house counsel of Geico insurance managing its West Palm Beach office for three years. This initial period of his career working as a lawyer representing insurance companies has proven invaluable to Mr. Benrubi today as he applies that knowledge to his cases on behalf of policyholders. In 1995 he left Geico because he decided that he wanted to represent individuals rather than insurance companies and joined Broad and Cassel in West Palm Beach for three years. He then joined a firm where he began his focus on insurance policyholder representation. He quickly became partner at that firm Liggio Benrubi P.A. where he remained for 18 years before launching his own firm the Law Office of Richard M. Benrubi P.A. and joining Rosenthal Levy Simon & Ryles as of counsel. Mr. Benrubi possesses a strong professional commitment to his clients because oftentimes his legal help is the only way they can get their lives back in order. I like helping people who have nowhere else to turn he says. These are people who are sick injured disabled need surgery. Their loved ones pass away and even though they have life insurance the insurance company denies their claim. I get great satisfaction from helping these people out. His work on behalf of policyholders has also resulted in cases that have changed Florida law. In early 2016 the Florida Supreme Court ruled in his favor in Paton v. Geico General Insurance Co. holding that billing records of opposing counsel are relevant as a guiding determination of plaintiff attorney fees. Another case Lutz v. Protective Life was a health-insurance class-action lawsuit charging that Protective Life had engaged in illegal premium charges. Mr. Benrubi commitment to policyholders is not restricted solely to his clients. He frequently lectures on insurance law and also writes an insurance column for the Florida Justice Association monthly publication FJA Journal. He enjoys the Martindale-Hubbell Law Directory top AV rating and has been named as a Super Lawyer 11 consecutive years by the Super Lawyers rating service. He has served as president of the Palm Beach County Justice Association and the Palm Beach Chapter of the American Board of Trial Advocates. In 2015 and 2016 he and his wife Karen S. Benrubi co-chaired the Palm Beach County Legal Aid Society Pro Bono Recognition Evening to honor lawyers who have provided valuable volunteer services to the indigent community. In his limited spare time Mr. Benrubi pursues an interest in music particular live blues acts travel and sports. First is the employee involved principally in selling a product or service which does not include making the product or rendering the service? Name: William Boyce Position: Member Education: Southwestern University School of Law Los Angeles California United States of America Southwestern University School of Law Los Angeles California United States of America Admitted: California 1982 Narrative: Bill is a very experienced trial attorney who has joined Grace Hollis after twenty years of practice as an equity partner in a statewide firm representing health care professionals. Bill was born in Fairmont West Virginia but he has lived in California since the age of six. His family moved west when Bill sister was placed under contract at Warner Brothers studios as a child actress. Bill soon followed in his sister footsteps appearing in movies and television from the age of six. Bill was featured in the movie High Noon and such television programs as I Love Lucy Dragnet and Superman. While attending law school from 1978 to 1981 Bill worked in Business Affairs and Finance at NBC in Burbank. He then became Director of Operations of IDC Services a diversified financial and production services company and later Vice President and General Manager of DISC Management Services a subsidiary of Lorimar Productions. Despite his busy work schedule Bill graduated from Southwestern University School of Law with high honors. Bill began his legal practice in 1981 defending products liability cases. Since 1983 he has specialized in the defense of medical professionals and hospital organizations. He has a national reputation as a trial attorney and is frequently asked to consult on and try cases in other states. Through twenty six years of continuous trial practice Bill has never lost a case. Bill lives in Thousand Oaks with his wife Sue. They have been married for twenty seven years and they are both active in serving their community. Bill serves on the Board of Directors of Hospice of the Conejo Community Conscience and Senior Concerns. He has also served as President of the Thousand Oaks Library Foundation and as an appointed member of various citizen advisory committees for the City of Thousand Oaks. Upon finishing his time in the service Specht continued his undergraduate studies in Ohio at the Cleveland State University eventually earning a BA degree in Political Science in 1995. From 2000 until 2014 Specht prosecuted some of the county s highest profile crime including but not limited to homocide rape crimes against the young aggravated robbery aggravated burglary illegal drugs and organized crime. In 2015 after unsuccessful bid for Judge in the Ashtabula Court of Common Pleas Specht stepped down as the Chief Assistant and took on a part time position in the same office as an assistant prosecutor. In March of 2015 Specht joined the staff of attorney at the Kurt Law Office located in Ashtabula County as a part time associate. Sperber represents California individuals and companies through all stages of the legal process from negotiation to litigation. Mr. Sperber specializes in employment law a field that encompasses nearly every issue that might arise between employers and employees from employment contracts to wage and hour issues to non-disclosure agreements to discrimination complaints. Mr. Sperber practice also includes general litigation consumer protection defamation and privacy. Mr. Sperber has successfully represented clients in numerous state and federal forums including the Superior Courts of California the California Labor Commissioner the California Unemployment Insurance Appeals Board the California Department of Fair Employment & Housing (DFEH) and the United States Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC). Mr. Sperber also represents clients in private arbitration and mediation. Mr. Sperber is a mediator for the EEOC the Berkeley Dispute Resolution Service and private parties. Prior to opening his own practice in 2000 Mr. Sperber practiced law at Littler Mendelson P.C. the largest labor and employment law firm in the United States. While at Littler Mendelson Mr. Sperber advised employers on myriad employment-related issues including anti-discrimination laws executive employment contracts arbitration agreements employee handbooks unfair competition hiring policies and practices employee privacy and premises liability. Additionally Mr. Sperber conducted investigations and litigated on behalf of his clients which ranged from small businesses to Fortune 100 companies. Mr. Sperber also clerked for the Oakland City Attorney the San Francisco Employment Law Center and Simpson Aherne & Garrity P.C. (now Simpson Garrity & Innes P.C.) an AV-rated law firm that represents management in labor and employment litigation. Mr. Sperber is admitted to practice before the California Supreme Court all Courts of Appeal and Superior Courts as well as the United States District Court for the Northern District of California.
